conditions: The pointer refers to the stated array object, the arithmetic uses the specified unit offset without overflow, and the unary indirection in question would be evaluated.
limitations: This covers the two specified pointer movements and evaluated indirection. Pointer subtraction, equality, scalar-object treatment, and representation or address adjacency have their own rules.
Scope is the exact N3220 C2y working draft. Published ISO text and observed implementation behavior require separate evidence.

triggers: Correction of the draft or passage, exact bytes drift, contrary primary evidence, or a superseding edition requiring a separate claim.

statement: WG14 draft N3220 describes adding one to a pointer to the last element of an array to form its one-past pointer, and subtracting one from that one-past pointer to return to the last element. It states that a one-past result cannot be the operand of an evaluated unary `*`.
